correctness.rationale: The three outward support normals sum to zero, hence the equilateral support triangle inradius equals the mean of three polygon support values and area equals 3sqrt(3)rho^2. For a regular n-gon h(phi)=R cos distance(phi,2pi Z/n). When 3|n the three values coincide, giving rho range R cos(pi/n) to R. Otherwise their phases modulo vertex period are t,t+Delta/3,t-Delta/3; on the reduced |t|<=Delta/6 chamber rho=C_n cos t with C_n=R(1+2cos(2pi/(3n)))/3. This proves all orientations and endpoint identities, and leads to n^-2 spread with factor-nine leading ratio. Independent evaluation of all original polygon vertex support functions for 6200 angles across 3<=n<=64 confirmed both closed ranges, not used as proof.
residual_risks: Equilateral support triangles only, regular Euclidean convex n-gons; no non-equilateral global minimizing assertion for 3 not dividing n.
